title: Traumatic cardiac tamponade after a penetrating chest wound

guidelineVersions: ERC Guidelines 2025: Special Circumstances in Resuscitation (Resuscitation, October 2025)
Resuscitative thoracotomy multisociety consensus (Wien Klin Wochenschr, 2026)

related.why: Blunt chest trauma with flail chest, where tamponade is the differential
The primary survey and tension pneumothorax, the other obstructive cause of shock

brief.role: Core surgical trainee on the trauma team
brief.scenario: Mr Euan Stobart, 45, arrives with a single stab wound just left of the sternum. He is pale, anxious and hypotensive.
brief.task: Answer the examiner's questions on your assessment and immediate management.

beforeYouWalkIn.frame: Wound in the cardiac box plus shock is tamponade until proven otherwise; the fix is surgical.
beforeYouWalkIn.trap: Treating needle pericardiocentesis as the treatment, or sending him to CT.
beforeYouWalkIn.firstMove: "This is likely cardiac tamponade. I need the trauma team leader and cardiothoracic surgeon now."

grid.label: Recognition
grid.fail: Diagnoses hypovolaemia or pneumothorax alone without considering tamponade.
grid.pass: Stab wound in the cardiac box with hypotension, raised neck veins and muffled heart sounds: cardiac tamponade.
grid.high: Knows the triad is often incomplete, and excludes tension pneumothorax clinically (trachea, breath sounds).

grid.label: Primary survey and eFAST
grid.fail: Delays for chest X-ray or CT, or omits ultrasound.
grid.pass: ABCDE with oxygen, two large-bore cannulae, bloods and cross-match, and eFAST including the pericardial view.
grid.high: Knows a negative pericardial view can mislead if blood drains into the left pleura; a haemothorax should raise suspicion.

grid.label: Escalation and definitive care
grid.fail: Manages alone or waits to see the response before calling for help.
grid.pass: Calls trauma team leader and cardiothoracic surgeon immediately; theatre now for sternotomy or thoracotomy and repair.
grid.high: Activates the major haemorrhage protocol and moves him straight to theatre without CT.

grid.label: Pericardial anatomy
grid.fail: Cannot describe the layers of the pericardium.
grid.pass: Fibrous pericardium outside; serous pericardium with parietal and visceral layers; blood collects between them.
grid.high: The fibrous layer cannot stretch acutely, so a small volume causes tamponade; phrenic nerves run on its lateral surface.

grid.label: Role of pericardiocentesis
grid.fail: Offers pericardiocentesis as definitive treatment, or stands theatre down after it.
grid.pass: Temporising only, when surgery cannot happen immediately; ultrasound-guided; theatre still needed.
grid.high: Clotted blood may not aspirate, so failure proves nothing; it must never delay transfer to theatre.

grid.label: If he arrests
grid.fail: Continues standard CPR alone or attempts a needle first.
grid.pass: Resuscitative thoracotomy to release the tamponade, if within 15 minutes of arrest with a trained team and kit.
grid.high: Clamshell approach; opens the pericardium in front of the phrenic nerves and controls the wound with a finger.

failures.move: Attributing shock to blood loss alone.
failures.consequence: Fluids are given while the heart cannot fill.

failures.move: Sending him for CT or waiting for a chest X-ray.
failures.consequence: He deteriorates away from the resuscitation room and theatre.
The cardiac wound is left unrepaired and tamponade recurs.

failures.move: Continuing CPR alone in traumatic arrest from tamponade.
failures.consequence: Chest compressions cannot fill a tamponaded heart.

recovery.line: To correct that: it buys time; the wound needs surgical repair.
A negative scan with a haemothorax doesn't exclude a cardiac injury.

knowledge.fact: Penetrating wound in the cardiac box with shock: tamponade until proven otherwise. The triad is often incomplete.
Fibrous pericardium cannot stretch acutely; the phrenic nerves run on its lateral surface.
Pericardiocentesis only when thoracotomy cannot be done; it does not remove clot or close the wound.
Traumatic arrest from tamponade after penetrating injury: resuscitative thoracotomy within 15 minutes if the team, kit and setting allow; clamshell preferred.

reveals.trigger: Candidate examines neck, chest and heart sounds
reveals.finding: Distended neck veins, muffled heart sounds. Trachea central, breath sounds equal.
Pericardial fluid with right ventricular collapse in diastole. No free abdominal fluid.
